1→# thos
     2→
     3→**the orchestrator you never knew you needed**
     4→
     5→A visual orchestration layer for [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code). Not another IDE — a UI that sits on top of the terminal-based agents you already use, solving the real friction of working with them day-to-day.
     6→
     7→## The Problem
     8→
     9→AI coding agents are powerful, but the experience of *using* them has real gaps:
    10→
    11→- **You lose track of what's happening.** Multiple agents running across tasks, and you're tab-switching and scrolling terminals to figure out who's doing what. The visibility problem compounds fast.
    12→
    13→- **Agents are smart but have the memory of an infant.** Your workflows are specific to you — your project structure, your preferences, your domain knowledge. The agent doesn't retain any of it between sessions. You end up re-explaining the same context over and over. A static CLAUDE.md helps, but it doesn't learn from your conversations or evolve with your codebase.
    14→
    15→- **Your machine is the bottleneck.** You have a laptop, not a build server. Agents want to compile, test, run — and your local machine can't keep up.
    16→
    17→- **Undoing things is painful.** Agent makes a wrong turn, and now you're doing forensics. Better change tracking, rollback, and context management should be table stakes — not an afterthought.
    18→
    19→- **Task management is manual.** Coordinating what gets done, in what order, across which agents — that's on you, in your head, with no tooling to help.
    20→
    21→## What thos Is
    22→
    23→thos is a UI wrapper around Claude Code. Terminals are fine — but when you're orchestrating work across agents, you need something more visual.
    24→
    25→Think of it as a control plane:
    26→
    27→- **Agent dashboard** — see what every agent is doing, in real time, at a glance
    28→- **Persistent memory** — agents that learn from your conversations and retain domain knowledge across sessions. Not just saved prompts — context that evolves with your codebase and workflows, so the first time you explain something is the last time.
    29→- **Change management** — track, diff, and roll back agent-generated changes with confidence
    30→- **Task orchestration** — assign, sequence, and track work across agents
    31→- **Remote access** — web UI accessible via localhost, with the option to expose over your network as needed
    32→
    33→## What thos Is Not
    34→
    35→- **Not an IDE.** VS Code, Cursor, Zed — these are well-engineered. thos doesn't compete with them; it complements them.
    36→- **Not a terminal replacement.** The terminal is the execution layer. thos is the visibility and coordination layer on top.
    37→- **Not a general agent framework.** Focused on Claude Code first. Breadth comes later, if it makes sense.
    38→
    39→## Prior Art
    40→
    41→Similar space as [superset.sh](https://superset.sh) and [Conductor](https://conductor.sh) — tools that recognize the gap between raw agent capability and the UX of actually orchestrating agent work.
    42→
    43→## Architecture
    44→
    45→### WebSocket relay server (`server/ws.ts`)
    46→
    47→A standalone WebSocket server on port 9900, started alongside Next.js via `concurrently`. Two connection families:
    48→
    49→- **`/browser`** — React dashboard connects here. Supports multiple tabs simultaneously.
    50→- **`/claude/:agentId`** — each Claude CLI connects here (passed as `--sdk-url`).
    51→
    52→The server acts as a relay: browser spawns agents, the server launches `claude` inside tmux sessions, and all CLI NDJSON messages are forwarded to the browser as `{ type: "relay", agentId, message }`.
    53→
    54→### Session persistence (`server/session-store.ts`)
    55→
    56→Agent state and full message history are persisted to `$TMPDIR/thos-sessions/<agentId>.json`. This means:
    57→
    58→- **Page refresh** restores all conversations — the server replays `message_history` to each connecting browser.
    59→- **Server restart** restores agents from disk. Agents that were active are marked `"disconnected"` and relaunched when a browser reconnects.
    60→- **Multiple browser tabs** see the same state — `sendToBrowser` iterates a `Set<WebSocket>` of all connected browsers.
    61→
    62→Writes are **debounced** (150ms) for high-frequency streaming events and **synchronous** for critical state changes (spawn, result, status transitions). On `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`, all agents are flushed to disk before tmux sessions are killed.
    63→
    64→### CLI resilience
    65→
    66→| Scenario | Behavior |
    67→|----------|----------|
    68→| CLI process crashes | Status becomes `"disconnected"`, browser sees "CLI disconnected — attempting reconnect..." |
    69→| Browser reconnects | Server relaunches dead agents via `claude --resume --sdk-url ...` if they have a `sessionId` |
    70→| Message sent while CLI is down | Queued in `pendingMessages[]`, flushed when CLI WebSocket reconnects |
    71→| CLI reconnects | Browser sees "CLI reconnected", queued messages are delivered |
    72→
    73→### Agent status lifecycle
    74→
    75→```
    76→idle → spawning → connected ⇄ thinking → done
    77→                      ↓                    ↑
    78→                 disconnected ─────────────┘
    79→                      ↓          (relaunch)
    80→                    error
    81→```
    82→
    83→- `idle` — no process, ready to spawn
    84→- `spawning` — tmux session created, waiting for CLI WebSocket
    85→- `connected` — CLI connected, `system/init` received
    86→- `thinking` — waiting for assistant response
    87→- `done` — CLI WebSocket closed cleanly
    88→- `disconnected` — CLI WebSocket dropped unexpectedly (crash, kill, server restart)
    89→- `error` — unrecoverable failure
    90→
    91→### Message flow
    92→
    93→```
    94→Browser                    WS Server                    Claude CLI
    95→  │                           │                            │
    96→  │──spawn(prompt)──────────▶│                            │
    97→  │                           │──tmux new-session──────▶│
    98→  │◀──spawned(agentId)───────│                            │
    99→  │                           │◀──hook_response───────────│
   100→  │                           │──user(prompt)────────────▶│
   101→  │◀──relay(system/init)─────│◀──system/init──────────────│
   102→  │◀──relay(assistant)───────│◀──assistant─────────────────│
   103→  │◀──relay(control_request)─│◀──control_request──────────│
   104→  │──control_response───────▶│──control_response─────────▶│
   105→  │◀──relay(result)──────────│◀──result────────────────────│
   106→  │                           │                            │
   107→  │  (page refresh)           │                            │
   108→  │──connect /browser────────▶│                            │
   109→  │◀──agent_list─────────────│                            │
   110→  │◀──message_history────────│  (replays all stored msgs) │
   111→```
   112→
   113→### Key files
   114→
   115→| File | Purpose |
   116→|------|---------|
   117→| `server/ws.ts` | WebSocket relay server — agent lifecycle, message routing, multi-browser, persistence integration |
   118→| `server/session-store.ts` | File-based JSON persistence with debounced/sync writes |
   119→| `hooks/use-websocket.ts` | React hook — connection management, message processing, dedup, reconnect handling |
   120→| `lib/types.ts` | Shared TypeScript types for all message protocols |
   121→| `components/dashboard/agent-sidebar.tsx` | Agent list with status dots |
   122→| `components/dashboard/chat.tsx` | Chat interface for the active agent |
   123→| `components/dashboard/status-bar.tsx` | Connection and agent status indicator |
   124→
   125→## Status
   126→
   127→Early stage. Solving my own problems first, seeing where it goes from there.
   128→
   129→---
   130→
   131→Built by [@chiumax](https://github.com/chiumax)
